correctness.rationale: Proof reduces separating automata exactly to noncommuting power permutations. Power-generated subgroups are normal and their elementwise centralization characterizes identities. For m>=5 all nontrivial normal subgroups contain nonabelian A_m. Small groups S3 and S4 are classified explicitly, and exponent jumps characterize prime powers. Sharp length bounds follow. Independent exhaustive permutation checks in degrees 2..6 cover 7384 exponent-residue pairs, with additional explicit witnesses; finite checks are not offered as proof of the infinite claim.

value.rationale: Classifies all two-block cyclic conjugate pairs, a natural infinite family in reversible word separation directly connected to contemporary permutation-identity research. The exact allowed minimal degrees are the prime powers, with exceptional m=3,4 behavior and sharp optimal length for every attainable degree; this is structural, not a routine recomputation of the prior S3 example. The theorem gives explicit benchmark families but no claim about unrestricted automata or general word separation.
